After moving from self-hosted git to GitLab, one team found the CI, namespacing and issue tracking "truly great and well thought of." But they lost entire days unable to deploy because CI workers (which they host) didn't run, so no artifacts were built. Nearly every day pushes took minutes, versus seconds on GitHub.
"I love GitLab, and I use a private instance at work, but I won't use it to store my public projects for one sole reason: you can't hide your email address shown in commits."

Migrating repos is straightforward: the GitHub importer brings over repo data, description, issues, pull requests, wiki pages, milestones, labels, release notes, review comments, cross-references and private/public visibility.
A self-described broke amateur dev praised GitLab: the team sent them a t-shirt and stickers even though they couldn't pay. They value being able to use either GitLab.com or a self-run instance.

During the import spike after the GitHub acquisition news, multiple users reported getting 502 errors on GitLab. One said "GitLab is crashing... but Bitbucket is up," recommending Bitbucket's code review and CI as an alternative.
A user wants to move to GitLab but can't: someone has held their username "labster" for over two years as an empty group, with no way to contact them. "So for now, it looks like I'm stuck on Github."
One user values that GitLab is open source at its core: anybody can run their own instance, and if the company moves in a direction the community dislikes, it can be forked.
A user has run GitLab self-hosted in a VM using the TurnKey Linux GitLab appliance "since forever."
"I've loved the product for about two years now, so curious to see how this plays out" — a long-time user reacting to the database incident.

On self-hosted GitLab (GLE), backups broke starting in 8.15. A "readable" date stamp was added to the backup filename without proper testing, causing many issues. It was somewhat fixed, but the user still saw issues in 8.16.
A user noticed the outage while pushing code earlier that day, but encouraged the team: "You guys are doing a great job."
Reacting to GitLab's admission that none of its 5 backup/replication methods were working: this "is no way to be running a public service with customer data."

One commenter calls GitLab's people incredible, open and transparent. But the incident shows why you shouldn't entrust a cloud service to keep your data safe: "My backups work. I know they work, because I run them and I test them."

A user switched their personal projects and 3 organizations they advise from GitHub to GitLab over the past year. GitLab won them with its data centers in Asia and Europe; GitHub is "extremely slow in Asia."

"I love Gitlab but sadly, quite a lot of services that offer free accounts for open source projects (TravisCI comes to mind), generally don't integrate with Gitlab. It's one of the few reasons why I am still using Github."
A user recently started using GitLab as their main portfolio and likes the company's openness and its services and ecosystem.
